name: Fred A. Willard
role: Stock inspector, deputy U.S. marshal and Billings County sheriff
bio: Fred A. Willard came to Medora in June 1885 as the stock inspector appointed by the Montana stock association, and in July he went to Fargo for his commission as a deputy U.S. marshal. Over the next year and a half he recovered strayed horses for ranchers, posted notices against firing guns in public, took a rifle away from a drunken man in December 1885, and inspected at the slaughter-house. He was named for sheriff on the Billings County ticket in March 1886 and elected in April, and his bond as sheriff was accepted in May. In October 1886 he and John Goodall went to Oliver County to quarantine a herd believed to have pleuro-pneumonia; that month he was renominated for sheriff, and he was re-elected in November. In December 1886 he brought George Myers back to Medora on a warrant sworn out by the Montana Stockgrowers' Association.
